In 1619 Praetorius used “screaming pipe” for a similar instrument. Surviving consorts are in Berlin and Prague, with one instrument in Vienna; a late seventeenth-century Naumburg collection contained a complete set of originals from sopranino down to bass. The Rauschpfeife is a woodwind used in Europe in the 16th and 17th centuries, an aerophone, Hornbostel–Sachs number 422.111. Its construction is similar to that of the crumhorn and the cornamuse: it is a wooden double-reed instrument with the reed enclosed in a wind cap, and the player blows through the opening at the top of the cap to sound it. The bore is conical, the reed vibrates without restriction inside the cap, the volume is very large, and it is suited to playing outdoors.
